sections.name: eslintConfig
sections.title: Project lint rules
sections.what: Sets the project's rules: the engine folder may only import other engine files, the app, components and ui folders must use design tokens instead of raw hex colours, and the ui folder may not import database code. It also lists folders the lint skips, such as build output and the deliberately bad fixture.
sections.why: The comments say the layering comes from ARCHITECTURE.md and a test checks it too.
sections.watch_out: The fixture folder is skipped on purpose, and removing that ignore would make the check that proves the rules catch bad code fail.

summary: Lint configuration: the standard Next.js checks plus project rules that keep the app's layers separate and its colours consistent.
purpose: Catch architecture and style breaks whenever the code is linted.
why: The comments say the layering comes from ARCHITECTURE.md and is also enforced by a test.
how: 1) Load the framework rule sets. 2) Add layer rules for the engine folder, for pages and components, and for the ui folder. 3) Add the colour rule for components. 4) Skip build output and the deliberately bad fixture folder.
outputs: Lint errors with messages telling the developer what to do instead.
risks: A changed pattern can quietly allow forbidden imports. Skipped folders are not linted at all.
debug: If a colour error appears, use a design token. If an import is blocked, move the logic to a service as the message says. If a new folder is not checked, check the file patterns.
